IndusEquip Corporation - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the IndusEquip Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to register and then press the star key followed by the 1 on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star followed by 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss IndusEquip Corporation's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on IndusEquip Corporation's performance for Q3. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. First, we've navigated a challenging macroeconomic landscape that has unevenly impacted end-market demand, with pressures in cyclical areas offset by strength in secular growth segments. Second, our inventory levels are well-managed through advanced strategies that keep us lean and responsive. Third, we've made impressive strides in reducing lead times for our key products and components, enhancing our delivery reliability. Fourth, we've continued to gain market share in critical regions and segments. Fifth, favorable price-cost dynamics have supported healthy margin expansion despite input volatility. Sixth, demand trends in our core end markets—construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing—show resilience and selective acceleration. Seventh, we delivered strong total revenue growth year-over-year. And eighth, revenue performance was solid across geographic regions, with particular strength in North America and Asia-Pacific.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Sarah. Turning to our financial performance, IndusEquip Corporation reported total revenue of $2.85 billion for the quarter, representing an 8% increase year-over-year from $2.64 billion in Q3 2023. This topped our guidance and reflects robust execution amid a bifurcated environment. Drilling deeper, equipment sales drove the bulk at about 67% of the mix, up 6% YoY, while aftermarket parts and services grew faster at 15% to $950 million, now 33% of total revenue. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.42, ahead of expectations. Gross margins expanded to 28.2%, benefiting from raw material deflation and pricing discipline. Operating expenses were controlled at $410 million, yielding operating income of $410 million and net income of $285 million, or $1.42 per share.

Let me unpack the key drivers behind these results, starting with the impact of macroeconomic factors on end-market demand, which has dominated our narrative this quarter. We're steering through elevated interest rates—the Fed's terminal rate near 5.25-5.50% has raised financing hurdles for OEMs in capital-heavy sectors like construction and mining. U.S. industrial CapEx, per the ISM Manufacturing PMI at 47.8 in September, contracted, leading to a 12% drop in non-residential construction orders sequentially. Our hydraulic excavators and telehandlers mirrored Caterpillar exposure, with book-to-bill dipping to 0.85x from 1.1x. Globally, ECB rates at 4.25% stalled European projects under fiscal constraints. On the flip side, easing inflation—U.S. CPI at 2.4% YoY—stabilized costs, fueling aftermarket growth.

Industrial production tells a mixed tale: U.S. IP up just 1.2% YoY pressured general industrial demand, with our CNC machining centers and assembly automation down 7% in orders from consumer discretionary pullbacks. But semiconductors and electronics surged 22%, driven by AI fabs from TSMC and Intel—our precision wafer handlers saw backlog balloon 25% to $1.2 billion. Geopolitics spiked oil to $75/barrel via OPEC+ cuts and Red Sea issues, lifting oil & gas CapEx 14% per Rystad, boosting our drilling components 18% YoY. Renewables countered with U.S. IRA incentives pushing wind nacelle orders 30%, though Europe faced gas price headwinds.

Regionally: North America, 52% of revenue, grew 10% on reshoring—CHIPS Act fueled 20% uptake in palletizers and AGVs from Rust Belt plants, despite CRE weakness trimming HVAC 5%. Europe, 25%, dipped 3% on 0.5% GDP and energy woes; auto OEMs like Volkswagen delayed presses, but battery lines gained 15%. Asia-Pacific, 18%, jumped 12% via China's $1.4 trillion stimulus for steel revamps—continuous casters up 25%—plus India's rail orders at $200 million. Rest of World, 5%, rose 16% on Australian and LatAm mining for copper.

We've countered with Industry 4.0, grabbing 40% share in smart factories via IoT predictive platforms akin to Siemens MindSphere, lifting software to 12% of mix. Electrification like 48V hybrids cuts fuel 25%, winning Deere and Komatsu specs. Diversification shifted semiconductors to 22%, renewables to 18%, trimming cyclicality. SG&A at 14.5%, $300 million buybacks signal confidence. Q4 orders eyed at +5-7% assuming Fed cuts; backlog $4.2 billion at 1.6x book-to-bill, FCF conversion 45%, R&D 5.2%.

Shifting to market share gains, we've expanded net 180 basis points YoY to 7.2% globally in core CNC, robotics, and presses—strongest since 2021. North America gained 210 bps to 12.1% on reshoring ($200 billion YTD), with $450 million Ford EV contract displacing Fanuc via 22% uptime edge; aftermarket up 15%, 65,000 IoT assets. Europe +140 bps to 6.8% on Green Deal—ElectroServe presses 40% greener won Airbus, VW. APAC mixed: China -50 bps to 4.1% from locals, but India +320 bps to 5.6% via Tata, Reliance. LatAm +80 bps on Vale mining. $350 million R&D in AI defect detection, modular TCO cuts fuel gains; FY25 eyes 150-200 bps more.

Price-cost dynamics powered margins: ASPs +6.2% outran 2.8% input inflation by 250 bps. Construction hikes 7-8%, automation 5.5%. Steel (45% basket) at $750/ton down 4% QoQ, aluminum $2,450/ton -15% off peaks, copper $9,200. NA pricing strong, Europe countered 8% steel premiums with 6% hikes, APAC hedged copper. Gross margins +230 bps to 28.5%, EBITDA 19.2%. Hedged 70% steel, diversified to Nucor; value engineering saved 8% on booms. Aftermarket 45% margins, electrification mix shift.

Total revenue context: Q3 $2.85 billion +8%, full-year tracking $10.5 billion +12-14%. NA 52% +19% on CHIPS/EV, EMEA 24% +9% wind, APAC 20% +21% China/India, ROW 4% +11%. Pricing 7-9%, Nexus platform $800 million orders, localized sourcing.

Revenue by geography aligns: NA $1.14 billion +18% on PMI>50, CNC +25%; EMEA $595 million +4% gas turbines +12%; APAC $521 million +11% India +28%; ROW $223 million +8% mining. Backlog $8.2 billion.

We remain committed to disciplined capital allocation and maximizing shareholder value.

Now, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've optimized manufacturing, supply chains, and service amid volatility. Inventory ended Q3 at $1.28 billion, +12% YoY but -4% QoQ: raw materials $520 million +18% hedged, WIP $410 million -8% on 15% throughput ramps, finished goods $350 million shifted to high-margin automation. Turns 4.7x vs. peers 4.1x, DIO 78 days below 85 median, ratio 18%. NA 5.2x on IIJA, EMEA 4.5x wind, APAC 4.0x China soft, LatAm stable. AI demand sensing (92% accuracy w/Palantir), VMI 35% cuts leads 25 days, Smart Stock IoT/digital twins pivoted 15% production. Diversified suppliers, targeting 5.5x turns; added 120 bps to 32.5% margins.

Lead times averaged 14 weeks -22% QoQ, 35% YoY: TitanPro CNC 12 weeks 1.4x btb, components 8 weeks dual-sourced, magnets 10 weeks. NA 13 weeks reshoring, EMEA 15 weeks buffered, APAC 16 weeks friendshoring. $150 million Resilience 2.0: AI forecasting, digital twins 88% utilization, Nucor/JFE contracts. On-time 96% vs. 85% industry.

Demand trends: Construction 42% rev +22% NA IIJA excavators 78% util, EMEA +2% telehandlers, APAC India loaders. Mining 28% +8% LatAm copper trucks +25%, APAC autonomous 18%; BEV pilots. Ag 18% +5% NA tractors +12%, Brazil +14%. Manufacturing 12% +15% CHIPS palletizers +30%. Book-to-bill 1.25x, orders $1.8 billion +12%, NA +16%, APAC +9%.

We're leveraging digital tech for excellence and prioritizing employee safety.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Raj Singh, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Raj Singh (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation in AI, ML, robotics, and IoT for predictive maintenance, operations optimization, and performance boosts. Our IndusFlex AI-driven CNC series is transforming the market, capturing share with 22% uptime gains, edge AI defect detection cutting scrap 18%, modular designs slashing TCO 25%, and IoT platforms like IndusConnect/MachineryConnect at 85% adoption, 65,000 assets. Electrification—BEV trucks, hybrids—aligns ESG, with Nexus cobots 30% faster cycles. $250-500 million R&D yields FactoryOS digital twins (25% less downtime), GreenForge energy AI. Targeting 20% share gains, 15 new SKUs, SaaS recurring.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Miller with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Miller (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the long-term impact of the new IndusFlex on your revenue and profitability?

Dr. Raj Singh (CTO):
Thanks, John. The IndusFlex is a game-changer, contributing 28% of Q3 bookings up from 15% YoY, with $800 million in orders via 30% cycle gains and predictive features cutting OEE losses 15%. Long-term, it drives 35% revenue mix by FY26, 32% margins vs. legacy 25%, recurring SaaS to 12-22%. Backlog conversion supports 25% Q4 lift, ROIC >15%, positioning for $200 billion automation capex.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for revenue growth in the coming year?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Emily, we guide FY25 revenue to $11.0-11.5 billion, 10-14% growth, with Q4 +5-7% orders, organic 9%, pricing 3-4%. Tailwinds: IIJA peak, mining $50 billion CapEx, precision ag 12% CAGR. Backlog $4.2-8.2 billion, services 35% at 45% margins. Risks recession/China balanced by diversification, FCF 45%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Ruiz (Morgan Stanley):
Can you discuss your plans for expanding your global footprint?

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
David, expansion is core: $150-250 million capex for Spartanburg, Pune JV, Ohio/Germany AS/RS. Localizing 60-70% NA/APAC cuts leads 35-40%, targets 10% India share FY26. Nearshoring Mexico/Vietnam, Frankfurt hub. Reshoring/PLI/Green Deal fuel 12% CAGR markets, $450 million frames like Foxconn.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim (Barclays):
How are you managing rising energy costs?

Lisa Patel (COO):
Laura, energy up 8% Europe we offset via GreenForge AI (20% savings), value engineering 3-5% COGS, hedging 60-70%, capacity 85-88%. Electrification pilots regenerative braking 30% OPEX cut, digital twins optimize. Diversified sourcing, AS/RS capex buffers; margins +230 bps despite.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in IndusEquip Corporation. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
